v.rationale: All three share a very similar shape: invokable controllers, a FormRequest that upper-cases and validates the currency, enum and Scope attributes, a lock with block() and a re-check inside the lock, a 30s failure backoff, and last-known fallback. None uses Cache::flexible for the dashboard, though the brief explicitly allows stale-while-revalidate. impl-1 had no functional bugs in probing, including team moves inside transactions. Its weaknesses are a vacuous 5-second stampede test and API routes living in web.php. impl-3 has the most robust invalidation (afterCommit, version bump, rollback-safe) and good deterministic lock tests. But it wrongly puts the exchange-rates endpoint behind auth and the web middleware, and the version scheme adds ceremony. impl-2 has a real invalidation bug: ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit plus getOriginal in saved() misses the old team on moves inside transactions. It also hand-rolls lock/remember for the dashboard and has no stampede test. Rank: impl-1 > impl-3 > impl-2.
